docs.title: NHRA mechanism models and game-theory maps
docs.text:
This repository provides stylised simulation and game-theory mapping to support governance reasoning about NHRA negotiations.

These models are not forecasts and should not be used to estimate budgets or clinical event counts.

Key outputs: - reports/ (HTML report, narrative summary) - outputs/ (plots, tables, diagrams) - diagrams/ (Mermaid and Graphviz sources)

docs.title: Context and local handover
docs.text: This project includes a context system under context/ that acts as the single source of truth for: - project intent and policy questions - modelling scope, limitations, and assumptions - abbreviations and reporting checklist guidance

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
• Build the shareable context pack:
python scripts/build_context_pack.py

This writes context/CONTEXT_PACK.md.

docs.title: Input traceability
docs.text:
Every model input in nhra_game_theory.v9.Params must be either: - anchored to a publicly retrievable source (URL), or - explicitly justified with a plausible range for sensitivity analysis.

To check:

python scripts/check_parameters_grounded.py

docs.title: design.md — Architecture, modelling approach, and evidence system (v21)
docs.text: Version: v21 Date: 2025-12-21

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The repository is designed as a model-based policy analysis toolchain with three pillars:

  1. Evidence / Context layer (public-only parameter grounding, provenance, checklists)
  2. Modelling layer (stage games + system dynamics; optional stochasticity; deterministic checks)
  3. Outputs layer (reports, plots, tables, diagrams; reproducible pipelines)

docs.title: Repo structure
docs.text:
• src/nhra_game_theory/ — core model library
  • tests/ — unit + property-like tests; coverage enforced
  • context/ — project intent, policy questions, parameter registry, provenance, glossaries
  • scripts/ — runnable pipelines (versioned; avoid “magic” by keeping scripts thin)
  • outputs/ — generated tables/plots
  • reports/ — rendered narrative reports (MD + HTML)
  • diagrams/ — mermaid + graphviz sources and rendered figures

docs.title: Parameter registry
docs.text:
context/04_parameter_registry.csv is the single source of truth for parameters.

Each parameter record includes: - value and units, - source type (primary, secondary, calibrated, assumed, normalisation), - a public URL and locator (page/table/section), - plausible range (low/high) and distribution (optional), - justification (required for assumptions).

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
scripts/check_parameters_grounded.py fails CI if: - a parameter is labelled primary or secondary and lacks a public URL, - an URL is not http/https, - a parameter is assumed but justification is insufficiently detailed, - range bounds are missing.

This ensures the model can be audited by external reviewers.

docs.title: 1) Stage games
docs.text:
A small set of two-player stage games represent strategic tensions, e.g.: - definition (what counts as “efficient”), - bargaining (cap/glide path), - cost shifting, - discharge coordination, - governance integration (UCCs etc), - compliance/audit incentives.

For each game, the code: - constructs payoff matrices from state variables (pressure, efficiency gap, discharge delay), - solves all Nash equilibria (pure + mixed) using enumeration / support methods, - selects equilibria for simulation using a configurable rule (e.g., welfare, risk-dominant).

docs.title: 2) System dynamics
docs.text:
A compact set of state variables evolve annually (or finer if needed), including: - NEP index and input-cost index (publicly sourced where available), - efficiency gap as cost-per-NWAU relative to NEP, - pressure, discharge delay, and flow proxies.

The dynamics support: - stochastic Monte Carlo runs (for robustness), - deterministic mean-field and fixed-point checks (equation solving for stability).

docs.title: Reports
docs.text: Reports are built from templates that: - introduce each results section in full sentences, - provide figure/table titles, captions, and abbreviations, - include a synthesis paragraph per section and an overall conclusion.

docs.title: Diagrams
docs.text:
Diagrams are maintained in source form: - diagrams/*.mmd (Mermaid) - diagrams/*.dot (Graphviz)

Render scripts generate publication-ready PNG/SVG.

docs.title: Reproducibility and CI
docs.text:
• Justfile provides a consistent local interface.
  • Snakefile provides a DAG for pipelines.
  • .github/workflows/ci.yml runs:
  • lint/format, tests, coverage gates, grounding checks, context pack build.

docs.title: Quality tooling
docs.text:
• Ruff (lint + format)
  • Pytest (+ Hypothesis properties)
  • Mypy (strict)
  • Pre-commit hooks
  • Tox
  • Dependabot

docs.title: Performance Profiling (Scalene)
docs.text: We use Scalene for high-performance CPU, GPU, and memory profiling.

docs.title: Profiling the Backtest Loop
docs.text:
To profile the recursive backtest:

LOGFIRE_SEND_TO_LOGFIRE=false PYTHONPATH=src scalene --cli --profile-all scripts/validation/recursive_backtest.py

Scalene will provide a detailed breakdown of time spent in v9.py (simulations) vs validation.py (logic).

docs.title: Diagrams
docs.text:
• User Mermaid sources: diagrams/mermaid_user/
  • Generated Mermaid: diagrams/mermaid_generated/
  • Graphviz sources: diagrams/graphviz_sources/
  • Converted outputs: diagrams/graphviz_from_mermaid/ and diagrams/mermaid_from_graphviz/
  • Rendered figures: outputs/v9/diagrams/

Render + convert:

PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/diagrams/render_all.py

docs.title: v8 hybrid model
docs.text:
The v8 hybrid model combines: - valuation divergence (NEP vs actual)

Note: In IHACPA’s ABF architecture, the NEP is an annual $ per NWAU price. Payments are derived by applying NEP to activity weights (NWAU) (plus adjustments). In this repo, NEP is used mainly to frame the efficient vs actual cost debate; many simulations run on normalised indices (NEP=1).

  • strategic games (bargain/define/cap/shift/govern/signal)
  • patient-flow proxies (occupancy, offload, ED≤4h)
  • a conservative harm index (comparative proxy only)

See: src/nhra_game_theory/legacy_engine.py and scripts/run_v8_all.py.

docs.title: Parameter registry
docs.text:
All model inputs for v9.Params are enumerated in:

  • context/04_parameter_registry.csv

docs.title: Rule
docs.text:
Each input must be either: 1) anchored to a publicly retrievable source (evidence_type: primary/secondary + URL), or 2) explicitly justified with a plausible range (evidence_type: assumed/calibrated/normalisation).

The registry is validated in CI:

python scripts/check_parameters_grounded.py

docs.title: Updating parameters
docs.text:
If you change v9.Params, regenerate the registry template then fill the evidence/jusification columns:

python scripts/make_parameter_registry_v20.py

docs.title: requirements.md — NHRA game-theory + system-dynamics modelling for RACMA (v21)
docs.text: Version: v21 Date: 2025-12-21 Audience: RACMA Policy & Advocacy Directorate; technical collaborators; reviewers (MJA)

docs.title: Problem statement
docs.text:
NHRA negotiations (2025–2030) require decision‑relevant insight into how vertical fiscal imbalance, activity‑based funding rules (NEP × NWAU), and interface constraints (aged care/NDIS/primary care) translate into operational risk and throughput failure (e.g., ED crowding, access block, ambulance offload delay). RACMA requires analysis that is:

  1. Mechanistically credible (causal story and incentives).
  2. Quantitatively disciplined (parameters traceable to public evidence or justified).
  3. Communicable (figures/tables that support both a RACMA position statement and an MJA original article).

docs.title: Primary users
docs.text:
• RACMA policy leaders: need an interpretable “negotiation dashboard” and mechanism-ranked asks.
  • MJA reviewers/readers: need transparent methods, parameter grounding, robustness checks.
  • Technical maintainers: need reproducible runs, CI, and a portable context pack.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Produce a model-based policy analysis of NHRA mechanisms, with explicit treatment of:
  2. NEP as annual $/NWAU and payments as NEP × NWAU (stylised where needed).
  3. input-cost growth vs NEP indexation drift (“valuation divergence”).
  4. strategic interactions (“games”) that drive cost shifting and governance fragmentation.
  5. Provide decision-relevant outputs:
  6. scenario comparisons (baseline vs policy packages),
  7. one-way + probabilistic sensitivity (where supported by evidence),
  8. equilibrium transparency (solving stage-game equilibria; deterministic checks for dynamics).
  9. Maintain a strict publicly retrievable evidence constraint: every non-trivial parameter must have
  10. a public URL with locator (page/table/section), or
  11. be explicitly labelled assumed with detailed justification + sensitivity bounds.

docs.title: In-scope
docs.text:
• Mechanism-level modelling of NHRA dynamics and incentives (Commonwealth vs state split levers).
  • Stage games (definition/bargaining/cost shifting/discharge coordination/governance/compliance).
  • System dynamics for pressure, discharge delay, and flow proxies.
  • Evidence registry and context pack generation.
  • Reproducible pipeline: just, snakemake, CI checks.

docs.title: Out-of-scope (for now)
docs.text:
• Full implementation of IHACPA NWAU XLSB calculators at runtime.
  • Jurisdiction‑specific hospital cost accounting.
  • Patient-level simulation; individual facility operational optimisation.

docs.title: Functional requirements
docs.text:
• FR1: Generate baseline trajectories (2025–2030) for:
  • pressure index, risk proxy, offload proxy, ED within‑4 proxy, efficiency gap.
  • FR2: Solve all Nash equilibria for each stage game at each year’s mean state.
  • FR3: Produce intervention scenarios reflecting RACMA “asks” (pooled funding, UCC governance integration, NEP alignment).
  • FR4: Produce evidence-linked figures and tables with captions and abbreviations.

docs.title: Non-functional requirements
docs.text:
• NFR1: Reproducible runs (seeded, deterministic options available).
  • NFR2: CI quality gates:
  • lint + formatting,
  • tests,
  • per-file coverage threshold,
  • evidence-grounding checks,
  • context pack build.
  • NFR3: Clear separation between model code and evidence/data.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• A1: just all and snakemake complete on a clean machine.
  • A2: scripts/check_parameters_grounded.py passes with public-only sources.
  • A3: Reports contain titled tables and figures with captions, abbreviations, and narrative synthesis.

docs.title: tasks.md — Roadmap and implementation plan (v21)
docs.text: Version: v21 Date: 2025-12-21

docs.title: Completed in v21
docs.text:
1. Added requirements.md, design.md, tasks.md as durable context artifacts.
  2. Extended the context pack to incorporate these artifacts.
  3. Tightened the grounding system to enforce publicly retrievable sources only.
  4. Updated developer workflows (just, snakemake) to build the context pack and run grounding checks.

docs.title: Completed in v23 — Reporting & Scenarios
docs.text:
1. Negotiation Dashboard: Added Effective Share Drift analysis and Ranked Intervention Table.
  2. Automated Methods: Implemented generate_methods_appendix.py and academic-style parameter exports.
  3. Refined Mechanisms: Resolved validation discrepancies; model now aligns with historical Rank #1 driver (Discharge Delay).

docs.title: Completed in v24/v25 — Evidence, Security & Release
docs.text:
1. Empirical API: Automated ingestion from AIHW MyHospitals API (ED performance).
  2. Bibliography Engine: Implemented academic citation manager with RIS/ENW/BIB exports.
  3. Security Hardening: Integrated Bandit security scanning, Mutmut mutation testing, and pinned requirements.lock.
  4. Audit Trails: Implemented Recorder for high-fidelity experiment provenance.
  5. Gold Master: Released v25.0.0 with optimized Docker environment.

docs.title: Completed in v26 — Codebase Maturity
docs.text:
1. Modern Tooling: Prepared dependencies for JAX acceleration.
  2. Community Standards: Added CONTRIBUTING/CODE_OF_CONDUCT and automated docs deployment.
  3. CI Hardening: Expanded testing matrix to Ubuntu/macOS/Windows.

docs.title: Next (v27) — Refactoring, Visualization & Deep Audit (Polishing the Core)
Core Refactoring
docs.text:
• Naming Convention: Rename opaque files (e.g., v9.py -> engine.py) for intuitive navigation.
  • Artifact Versioning: Implement timestamped output directories (outputs/experiments/YYYY-MM-DD/...) to prevent overwrites.

docs.title: Visualization & Polish
docs.text:
• Dynamic Animation: Generate GIFs/Videos of simulation trajectories (Pressure/Risk over time).
  • Publication Polish: Ensure all dashboard plots and exported figures meet high-impact journal standards (vector graphics, colorblind safe).

docs.title: Forensic Deep Dive
docs.text:
• Code Investigator: Systematically audit all legacy versions using AI agents to recover any missed logic or "ghost" features.
  • Library Review: Evaluate integration of new libraries (e.g., Mesa, PyGambit) vs current custom implementations.

docs.title: Future Track: Advanced Calibration & Validation
docs.text:
• Bayesian Inference: Move from TPESampler to fully Bayesian calibration (PyMC/Stan).
  • Counterfactual Validation: Test model against historical shocks not in training data.

docs.title: Future Track: Enhanced User Experience
docs.text:
• Interactive Scenarios: Allow policymakers to build intervention bundles via UI drag-and-drop.
  • Explainable AI: Add tooltips and narrative generation explaining why a specific outcome occurred.

docs.title: Future Track: Cloud & Cognitive Agents (On Hold)
docs.text:
• Simulation Visualization: Live visual feedback during execution.
  • LLM Agent Sophistication:
    • Debate Loop: Cth/State agents exchange structured arguments.
    • RAG Integration: Agents cite specific NHRA clauses from context/.
    • Multi-Agent Negotiation: Enable dynamic adaptation beyond static parameters.
  • Cloud Operations: Terraform/Docker hardening for AWS/Azure.
